editorial:
You meet Grace, a lonely girl who collects snails and loves her twin brother Gilbert. When their parents die, the two are split up and sent to different homes. Grace ends up with a kind but odd couple, while Gilbert lands with a strict religious family. The story follows Grace as she grows up, deals with loss, and slowly learns to believe in herself. The stop-motion animation looks handmade and full of heart, giving every scene a warm, slightly sad feeling. It is funny in a dark way, but also deeply touching.

The voice acting is strong, especially the lead who makes Grace feel real and lovable. The pacing is slow but steady, letting you sit with each moment. Some scenes may feel heavy, and the humor is not for everyone. If you enjoy emotional animated films with a quirky edge, this one is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Grace finally reunites with Gilbert after years apart. She discovers he has been struggling too, and their bond helps both of them heal. Grace also lets go of her hoarding habits and finds confidence in herself. The twist is that the snails she collected were never just pets; they symbolized her fear of moving forward. By the end, she chooses to live fully instead of hiding in her shell.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional animated stories with a quirky edge.
